verdict.rationale_short: The 30Y closed at 5.01% on May 27, formally confirming Day 2 and technically activating the high-conviction BUY framework — but overnight US-Iran military exchanges (US struck an Iranian military site; Iran's Revolutionary Guards retaliated against a US airbase) reversed oil's entire May 27 decline, with WTI +1.8% to $90 and Brent +2% to $96.07. With April PCE due at 8:30 AM ET (consensus core +3.3% YoY, highest since 2023) and S&P futures -0.2%, today is hold territory: manage existing positions with defined stops and do not add new broad-index longs until the oil-Iran and PCE double binary resolves.

bear_case: April PCE core at consensus +3.3% YoY would mark the highest reading since 2023 and a clear reacceleration from March's 3.2% — a print that would force Fed Chair Warsh to hold rates longer and likely push the 30Y back above 5.05%, voiding the Day 2 signal's strategic value within 24 hours of its confirmation. Iran's overnight military exchange with the US demonstrates that the deal is further away than markets priced in after May 27's oil decline; if Iran formally announces Strait of Hormuz restrictions in response to US strikes, Brent could retest $103+, triggering the full Step Aside scenario. If April PCE core exceeds 3.3% and the 30Y closes above 5.10% today, the HOLD call converts to Step Aside immediately; if SPX loses 7,460 on a daily close under that scenario, the BUY call is wrong.
